claim: Insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1) was reduced in failing mouse hearts post-myocardial infarction (MI).
source: We demonstrated that insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1) was reduced in failing mouse hearts post-myocardial infarction (MI) and failing human hearts.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mouse hearts post-MI as shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: IRS1 was reduced in failing human hearts.
source: We demonstrated that insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1) was reduced in failing mouse hearts post-myocardial infarction (MI) and failing human hearts.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from human heart samples as shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Mice manifesting severe cardiac dysfunction post-MI displayed elevated mir128-3p in the myocardium.
source: The mice manifesting severe cardiac dysfunction post-MI displayed elevated mir128-3p in the myocardium.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing increased mir128-3p levels in failing mouse hearts as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ischemia-upregulated mir128-3p promoted Irs1 degradation.
source: Ischemia-upregulated mir128-3p promoted Irs1 degradation.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays and protein expression data showing mir128-3p directly targets and reduces IRS1 as shown in Figure 2H-M.

claim: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 (MAPK7)-mediated CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein beta (CEBPβ) transcriptionally represses mir128-3p under hypoxia.
source: Using rat cardiomyocytes and human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, we elucidated that mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 (MAPK7, also known as ERK5)-mediated CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein beta (CEBPβ) transcriptionally represses mir128-3p under hypoxia.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP assays, luciferase reporter assays, and qPCR data showing CEBPβ binds to Pri-mir128-1 promoter and represses its transcription in a MAPK7-dependent manner as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Gene therapy-delivered cardiac-specific MAPK7 restoration impeded cardiac injury after MI.
source: Therapeutically, functional studies demonstrated gene therapy-delivered cardiac-specific MAPK7 restoration or overexpression of CEBPβ impeded cardiac injury after MI, at least partly due to normalization of mir128-3p.
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography, histology, and molecular data from AAV9-Mapk7 injected mice as shown in Figure 5.

claim: Overexpression of CEBPβ impeded cardiac injury after MI.
source: Therapeutically, functional studies demonstrated gene therapy-delivered cardiac-specific MAPK7 restoration or overexpression of CEBPβ impeded cardiac injury after MI, at least partly due to normalization of mir128-3p.
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography, histology, and molecular data from AAV9-Cebpb injected mice as shown in Figure 6.

claim: Inhibition of mir128-3p preserved Irs1 and ameliorated cardiac dysfunction post-MI.
source: Furthermore, inhibition of mir128-3p preserved Irs1 and ameliorated cardiac dysfunction post-MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography, histology, and molecular data from AAV9-Antimir128 injected mice as shown in Figure 7.

claim: Ischemic heart disease is a leading cause of mortality worldwide.
source: Ischemic heart disease is a leading cause of mortality worldwide (Benjamin et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Benjamin et al., 2019.

claim: The high prevalence of post-MI-associated heart failure remains despite advances in treatment.
source: Although significant advances in treatment have improved early survival after myocardial infarction (MI), such as bypass surgery, percutaneous coronary intervention, and thrombolytic therapy, the high prevalence of post-MI-associated heart failure (HF) remains (Sanchis-Gomar et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sanchis-Gomar et al., 2016.

claim: Promoting reliance on glucose under ischemic condition represents an indispensable adaptation with beneficial effects on survival in patients with ischemic heart disease.
source: Clinical studies suggest that promoting reliance on glucose under ischemic condition represents an indispensable adaption, which may have beneficial effects on survival in patients suffering from ischemic heart disease (Montessuit and Lerch, 2013; Ritterhoff and Tian, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Montessuit and Lerch, 2013 and Ritterhoff and Tian, 2017.

claim: Enhanced insulin-dependent glucose utilization in cardiomyocytes protects the heart against injury exacerbation at an early stage post-ischemia.
source: At an early stage post-ischemia, enhanced insulin-dependent glucose utilization in cardiomyocytes protects the heart against injury exacerbation (Nagoshi et al., 2011; Ussher et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nagoshi et al., 2011 and Ussher et al., 2012.

claim: Myocardial insulin resistance precedes and prophesies the onset and progression of HF during prolonged stress.
source: Conversely, myocardial insulin resistance precedes and prophesies the onset and progression of HF during prolonged stress (Aroor et al., 2012; Ciccarelli et al., 2011; Fu et al., 2016; Riehle and Abel, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Aroor et al., 2012; Ciccarelli et al., 2011; Fu et al., 2016; and Riehle and Abel, 2016.

claim: Impaired insulin signaling pathways in cardiomyocytes leads to loss of the major energy source, increased oxidative stress due to metabolic shift toward fatty acids, and deleterious cardiac remodeling.
source: Impaired insulin signaling pathways in cardiomyocytes leads to loss of the major energy source, increased oxidative stress due to metabolic shift toward fatty acids, and deleterious cardiac remodeling (Aroor et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2016; Tian and Abel, 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Aroor et al., 2012; Fu et al., 2016; and Tian and Abel, 2001.

claim: Human heart samples from subjects with advanced heart failure display an impaired IRS signaling and reduced plasma membrane SLC2A4.
source: Notably, human heart samples from subjects with advanced heart failure display an impaired IRS signaling and reduced plasma membrane SLC2A4 (Chokshi et al., 2012; Cook et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chokshi et al., 2012 and Cook et al., 2010.

claim: Myocardial loss of both IRS1 and IRS2 renders the heart more vulnerable to cardiac dysfunction in mice suffering from diabetes.
source: Myocardial loss of both IRS1 and IRS2 renders the heart more vulnerable to cardiac dysfunction in mice suffering from diabetes (Desrois et al., 2004; Qi et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Desrois et al., 2004 and Qi et al., 2013.

claim: Cardiac IRS1 and IRS2 double knockout mice displayed contractile dysfunction in early life.
source: In addition, cardiac IRS1 and IRS2 double knockout mice displayed contractile dysfunction in early life (Riehle et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Riehle et al., 2013.

claim: Impaired insulin sensitivity in ischemic myocardium is attributed to defective IRS1 function.
source: More importantly, impaired insulin sensitivity in ischemic myocardium is attributed to defective IRS1 function (Ciccarelli et al., 2011; Fu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ciccarelli et al., 2011 and Fu et al., 2016.

claim: Signature alterations of cardiac miRNAs have been implicated in cardiac hypertrophy, ischemic injury and heart failure.
source: Signature alterations of cardiac miRNAs have been implicated in a multitude of pathological processes, including cardiac hypertrophy, ischemic injury and heart failure (Caroli et al., 2013; Wojciechowska et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Caroli et al., 2013 and Wojciechowska et al., 2017.

claim: Silencing disease-prompted miRNAs using antagomiRs is considered as a potential therapeutic intervention for heart diseases.
source: Therefore, silencing disease-prompted miRNAs using antagomiRs is considered as a potential therapeutic intervention for heart diseases (van Rooij et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to van Rooij et al., 2008.

claim: Approximately 50% of human miRNAs are expressed from the introns of encoding transcripts.
source: Approximately 50% of human miRNAs are expressed from the introns of encoding transcripts, referred to as intronic miRNAs (Rodriguez et al., 2004), which are transcribed from the primary transcripts (Pri-miRNAs) along with their host genes (Saini et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rodriguez et al., 2004 and Saini et al., 2007.

claim: Mir128 promotes cardiomyocyte apoptosis during ischemia/reperfusion injury in rabbits.
source: Mir128 is an intronic miRNA, which promotes cardiomyocyte apoptosis during ischemia/reperfusion injury in rabbits (Zeng et al., 2016), while its loss advances mouse cardiac regeneration after MI (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zeng et al., 2016.

claim: Loss of mir128 advances mouse cardiac regeneration after MI.
source: Mir128 is an intronic miRNA, which promotes cardiomyocyte apoptosis during ischemia/reperfusion injury in rabbits (Zeng et al., 2016), while its loss advances mouse cardiac regeneration after MI (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2018.

claim: Four weeks post-MI, the mice displayed cardiac dysfunction exemplified by reduced fractional shortening (FS%), increased end-diastolic left ventricular internal diameter (dLVID) and end-systolic left ventricular internal diameter (sLVID).
source: Four weeks post-MI, the mice displayed cardiac dysfunction exemplified by reduced fractional shortening (FS%), increased end-diastolic left ventricular internal diameter (dLVID) and end-systolic left ventricular internal diameter (sLVID) (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Deleterious heart function was coupled to severe infarction and interstitial fibrosis in the non-infarct region.
source: Deleterious heart function was coupled to severe infarction and interstitial fibrosis in the non-infarct region (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by TTC staining and Masson's Trichrome staining shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: A significant number of genes responsible for glucose uptake and glycolysis were differentially expressed in the failing hearts post-MI.
source: We focused on analyzing the key genes involved in cardiac glucose metabolism, revealing that a significant number of genes responsible for glucose uptake and glycolysis were differentially expressed in the failing hearts post-MI (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: IRS1 was prominently decreased in failing hearts post-MI.
source: Among these altered genes, IRS1 was prominently decreased, which was validated by quantitative PCR (qPCR) and immunoblots (Figure 1F and G)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: The levels of other factors involved in glucose uptake (Insr, Slc2a4, and Slc2a1) were not significantly changed in failing hearts post-MI.
source: however, the levels of other factors involved in glucose uptake (Insr, Slc2a4, and Slc2a1) were not significantly changed (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: The insulin pathway was blocked after 4 week MI, as indicated by diminished phosphorylation of IRS1 and AKT in response to insulin stimulation.
source: As a result, the insulin pathway was blocked, as indicated by diminished phosphorylation of IRS1 and AKT in response to insulin stimulation after 4 week MI (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: IRS1, but not IRS2, was found to be downregulated in failing human hearts.
source: More importantly, cardiac insulin resistance is a feature of human HF (Aroor et al., 2012; Riehle and Abel, 2016), and IRS1, but not IRS2, was found to be downregulated in failing human hearts (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data from human heart samples shown in Figure 1I.

claim: IRS1 transcript level and protein expression were both decreased in adult rat cardiomyocytes (ARCMs) under prolonged hypoxic (1.5% O2) stress.
source: In line with observations from mouse and human heart samples, IRS1 transcript level and protein expression were both decreased in adult rat cardiomyocytes (ARCMs) under prolonged hypoxic (1.5% O2) stress (Figure 1J and K)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data from ARCMs shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: The levels of Insr, Slc2a4 and Slc2a1 were unchanged in ARCMs under prolonged hypoxic stress.
source: however, the levels of Insr, Slc2a4 and Slc2a1 were unchanged (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from ARCMs shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Insulin-stimulated plasma membrane-enriched SLC2A4 was significantly lower under long-term hypoxic condition.
source: Intriguingly, insulin-stimulated plasma membrane-enriched SLC2A4 was significantly lower under long-term hypoxic condition (Figure 1L).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data showing SLC2A4 membrane translocation in Figure 1L.

claim: Only mir128-3p displayed upregulation in the myocardium of long-term MI-induced failing hearts among three potential cardiac-abundant miRNAs (mir128-3p, mir144-3p and mir145-5p) targeting Irs1 3'UTR.
source: Among three potential cardiac-abundant miRNAs (mir128-3p, mir144-3p and mir145-5p) targeting Irs1 3'UTR, only mir128-3p displayed upregulation in the myocardium of long-term MI-induced failing hearts (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In situ hybridization confirmed an increased mir128-3p signal in ischemic myocardium.
source: In situ hybridization of mir128-3p further confirmed an increased signal in ischemic myocardium (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Increased mir128-3p was detected in ARCMs treated with prolonged hypoxia for 4–6 hr.
source: Consistently, increased mir128-3p was detected in ARCMs treated with prolonged hypoxia for 4–6 hr (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from ARCMs shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Endogenous Pri-mir128-1 level was augmented in sustained MI-induced failing hearts.
source: Endogenous Pri-mir128-1 level was augmented in sustained MI-induced failing hearts; however, no change of Pri-mir128-2 was detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: No change of Pri-mir128-2 was detected in sustained MI-induced failing hearts.
source: Endogenous Pri-mir128-1 level was augmented in sustained MI-induced failing hearts; however, no change of Pri-mir128-2 was detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Pri-mir128-1 was increased in ARCMs stressed by 4 and 6 hr hypoxia.
source: Consistently, Pri-mir128-1 was increased in ARCMs stressed by 4 and 6 hr hypoxia (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from ARCMs shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The seed sequence of mir128-3p is highly conserved among mouse, rat, and human.
source: The seed sequence of mir128-3p is highly conserved among mouse, rat, and human (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 2F.

claim: In silico screening detected two potential binding sites in the 3'UTR of human IRS1, one of which is highly conserved across mammalian species.
source: In silico screening detected two potential binding sites in the 3'UTR of human IRS1, one of which is highly conserved across mammalian species (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by in silico analysis and sequence alignment shown in Figure 2G.

claim: mir128-3p mimic caused a decrease in luciferase activity with respect to the control plasmid.
source: The validated mir128-3p mimic (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A) caused a decrease in luciferase activity with respect to the control plasmid; however, mutations that disrupt base pairing between mir128-3p and native IRS1 3'UTR upheld the luciferase expression (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Mutations that disrupt base pairing between mir128-3p and native IRS1 3'UTR upheld the luciferase expression.
source: The validated mir128-3p mimic (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A) caused a decrease in luciferase activity with respect to the control plasmid; however, mutations that disrupt base pairing between mir128-3p and native IRS1 3'UTR upheld the luciferase expression (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Enforced mir128-3p reduced both transcript and protein levels of IRS1 in ARCMs.
source: More convincingly, enforced mir128-3p reduced both transcript and protein levels of IRS1 in ARCMs (Figure 2I and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data from ARCMs shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: IRS1 3'UTR luciferase activity was enhanced by eliminating hypoxia-induced endogenous mir128-3p using validated mir128-3p antagomir.
source: Conversely, IRS1 3'UTR luciferase activity was enhanced by eliminating hypoxia-induced endogenous mir128-3p using validated mir128-3p antagomir (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B, Figure 2K).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2K and Figure 2—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Antagomir maintained IRS1 expression in ARCMs despite exposure to prolonged hypoxia.
source: As anticipated, antagomir maintained IRS1 expression in ARCMs albeit exposure of prolonged hypoxia (Figure 2L and M).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data from ARCMs shown in Figure 2L and M.

claim: Mir128-3p mimic impeded insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.
source: Mir128-3p mimic impeded insulin-stimulated glucose uptake (Figure 2N)
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2N.

claim: Antagomir showed retained glucose entry into ARCMs under hypoxia for 6 hr.
source: on the contrary, antagomir showed retained glucose enter into ARCMs under hypoxia for 6 hr (Figure 2O).
evidence: The claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2O.

claim: Only long-term hypoxia (4 and 6 hr) promoted transcription of Pri-mir128-1 in H9C2 cardiomyocytes.
source: Pri-mir128-1 promoter luciferase reporter assay targeting another putative TSS located between exon1 and exon2 of R3hdm1 illustrated that only long-term hypoxia (4 and 6 hr) promoted transcription of Pri-mir128-1 in H9C2 cardiomyocytes (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There are CEBP consensus binding sites in the Pri-mir128-1 promoter region, which are well conserved across species.
source: Using Ensembl and UCSC Genome Browser, we found that there are CEBP consensus binding sites in this region, which are well conserved across species (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cardiac-abundant Cebpb (encoding CEBPβ), but not Cebpa (encoding CEBPα), was decreased in C57BL/6N mouse hearts subject to prolonged ischemia for four weeks.
source: Interestingly, cardiac-abundant Cebpb (encoding CEBPβ), but not Cebpa (encoding CEBPα), was decreased in C57BL/6N mouse hearts subject to prolonged ischemia for four weeks (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Cebpb was reduced by long-standing hypoxic stress in ARCMs.
source: Similarly, Cebpb was also reduced by long-standing hypoxic stress in ARCMs (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from ARCMs shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CEBPβ overexpression minimized Pri-mir128-1 and mir128-3p expression, and consequently retained Irs1 transcript despite prolonged hypoxia.
source: We hypothesized that CEBPβ (LAP isoform, the most dominant and functioning isoform of CEBPβ) acts to transcriptionally repress mir128-3p, which was supported by CEBPβ overexpression minimizing Pri-mir128-1 and mir128-3p expression, and consequently retaining Irs1 transcript despite prolonged hypoxia, (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from CEBPβ overexpressing cells shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Rising Pri-mir128-1 was detected in Cebpb-knockdown ARCMs in response to short-term hypoxia for 2 hr.
source: Conversely, rising Pri-mir128-1 was detected in Cebpb-knockdown ARCMs in response to short-term hypoxia for 2 hr (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D, Figure 3F)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from Cebpb-knockdown ARCMs shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Irs1 transcript was downregulated due to the increased mature mir128-3p subsequent to Cebpb deficiency.
source: which consolidated a negative correlation between Cebpb and Pri-mir128-1 in hypoxic conditions. Subsequent to Cebpb deficiency, Irs1 transcript was downregulated due to the increased mature mir128-3p (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from Cebpb-knockdown ARCMs shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Pri-mir128-1 promoter luciferase activity was appreciably increased in H9C2 cardiomyocytes due to the loss of Cebpb.
source: Additionally, Pri-mir128-1 promoter luciferase activity was appreciably increased in H9C2 cardiomyocytes due to the loss of Cebpb (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Cebpb was not found to be related to Pri-mir128-2 in cardiomyocytes.
source: Of note, Cebpb was not found to be related to Pri-mir128-2 in cardiomyocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: Decreased Cebpb along with increased mir128-3p was shortly detected in Mapk7-deficient ARCMs after 2 hr hypoxia.
source: Indeed, decreased Cebpb along with increased mir128-3p was shortly detected in Mapk7-deficient ARCMs after 2 hr hypoxia (Figure 3J)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from Mapk7-deficient ARCMs shown in Figure 3J.

claim: MAPK7 overexpression preserved Cebpb and mir128-3p in a normal range even under long-term hypoxia for 6 hr.
source: however, MAPK7 overexpression preserved Cebpb and mir128-3p in a normal range even under long-term hypoxia for 6 hr (Figure 3K).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from MAPK7 overexpressing ARCMs shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Short-term hypoxia promoted binding of CEBPβ to Pri-mir128-1 promoter regions between exon1 and exon2 of R3hdm1 containing consensus CEBP binding sequence.
source: Short-term hypoxia promoted binding of CEBPβ to Pri-mir128-1 promoter regions between exon1 and exon2 of R3hdm1 containing consensus CEBP binding sequence; however, Mapk7 knockdown led to a remarkable reduction of association at various putative binding regions (−429 to −259; −2550 to −2383; −4047 to −3873 and −4176 to −4026 from intronic TSS) (Figure 3L, Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3L and Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Mapk7 knockdown led to a remarkable reduction of CEBPβ association at various putative binding regions in the Pri-mir128-1 promoter.
source: Short-term hypoxia promoted binding of CEBPβ to Pri-mir128-1 promoter regions between exon1 and exon2 of R3hdm1 containing consensus CEBP binding sequence; however, Mapk7 knockdown led to a remarkable reduction of association at various putative binding regions (−429 to −259; −2550 to −2383; −4047 to −3873 and −4176 to −4026 from intronic TSS) (Figure 3L, Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3L and Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Acute hypoxia-triggered CREB1 phosphorylation was inhibited by Mapk7 knockdown in ARCMs.
source: First, we screened potential MAPK7 downstream signaling factors responding to cardiac pathological stresses. Acute hypoxia-triggered CREB1 phosphorylation was inhibited by Mapk7 knockdown in ARCMs (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Short-term hypoxia-induced nuclei accumulation of activated CREB1 and CEBPβ was diminished as a result of Mapk7 knockdown.
source: Moreover, immunofluorescent staining confirmed that short-term hypoxia-induced nuclei accumulation of activated CREB1 and CEBPβ; however, their signals were diminished as a result of Mapk7 knockdown (Figure 3M).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: 2 hr hypoxia resulted in the physical association of phosphorylated CREB1 and CEBPβ.
source: Immunoprecipitation demonstrated that 2 hr hypoxia resulted in the physical association of phosphorylated CREB1 and CEBPβ; however, this affinity was unseen in the absence of MAPK7 (Figure 3N).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3N.

claim: The affinity between phosphorylated CREB1 and CEBPβ was unseen in the absence of MAPK7.
source: Immunoprecipitation demonstrated that 2 hr hypoxia resulted in the physical association of phosphorylated CREB1 and CEBPβ; however, this affinity was unseen in the absence of MAPK7 (Figure 3N).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3N.

claim: Creb1 knockdown in rat cardiomyocytes displayed decreased CEBPβ and reduced IRS1 expression following 2 hr hypoxia exposure.
source: To further evaluate whether CREB1, as a downstream effector of MAPK7, is also required for maintaining CEBPβ expression, we knocked down Creb1 in rat cardiomyocytes, which displayed decreased CEBPβ and reduced IRS1 expression following 2 hr hypoxia exposure (Figure 3O).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data from Creb1-knockdown cardiomyocytes shown in Figure 3O.

claim: The same effects detected from Mapk7-knockdown cells were rescued by CREB1 overexpression.
source: The same effects detected from Mapk7-knockdown cells were rescued by CREB1 overexpression (Figure 3O).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 3O.

claim: Mapk7-cko hearts promptly displayed detrimental function after one week MI, determined by decreased FS% and enlarged left ventricular chamber dimensions.
source: After one week, Mapk7-cko hearts promptly displayed detrimental function, determined by decreased FS% and enlarged left ventricular chamber dimensions; however, these impacts were not detected in Mapk7flox hearts, in which MAPK7 phosphorylation was triggered during short-term MI (Figure 4B, Figure 4—source data 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: These impacts were not detected in Mapk7flox hearts, in which MAPK7 phosphorylation was triggered during short-term MI.
source: After one week, Mapk7-cko hearts promptly displayed detrimental function, determined by decreased FS% and enlarged left ventricular chamber dimensions; however, these impacts were not detected in Mapk7flox hearts, in which MAPK7 phosphorylation was triggered during short-term MI (Figure 4B, Figure 4—source data 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by echocardiography and immunoblot data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: More elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) concentration was observed in Mapk7-cko mice one week post-MI.
source: Additionally, even though cardiac Troponin I (cTnI) level was comparable in Mapk7flox and Mapk7-cko serum 24 hr after ligation, more elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) concentration was observed in Mapk7-cko mice one week post-MI (Figure 4C), indicating MAPK7 loss led to augmented ligation-induced cardiac injury.
evidence: The claim is supported by LDH assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cardiac MAPK7 disruption contributed to larger infarct area.
source: Furthermore, cardiac MAPK7 disruption contributed to larger infarct area (Figure 4D) as well as more reactive myocardial fibrosis (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by TTC staining data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Cardiac MAPK7 disruption contributed to more reactive myocardial fibrosis.
source: Furthermore, cardiac MAPK7 disruption contributed to larger infarct area (Figure 4D) as well as more reactive myocardial fibrosis (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Masson's Trichrome staining data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Morphological analysis showed lower heart weight/body weight and cross-sectional area of cardiomyocytes in Mapk7-cko hearts compared to Mapk7flox hearts after MI.
source: Morphological analysis showed lower heart weight/body weight and cross-sectional area of cardiomyocytes in Mapk7-cko hearts compared to Mapk7flox hearts after MI (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: CREB1 phosphorylation was increased in Mapk7flox hearts in response to 1 week MI.
source: Strikingly, accompanied by the enhanced phosphorylated MAPK7 detected in Mapk7flox hearts, CREB1 phosphorylation was also increased in response to 1 week MI; however, this activation was not detected in Mapk7-cko hearts (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: CREB1 activation was not detected in Mapk7-cko hearts in response to 1 week MI.
source: Strikingly, accompanied by the enhanced phosphorylated MAPK7 detected in Mapk7flox hearts, CREB1 phosphorylation was also increased in response to 1 week MI; however, this activation was not detected in Mapk7-cko hearts (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Mapk7-cko hearts exhibited abridged Cebpb expression, correlated with augmented Pri-mir128-1 and mir128-3p compared to Mapk7flox hearts 1 week post-MI.
source: Noticeably, in agreement with observations obtained from the failing hearts induced by 4 week MI, Mapk7-cko hearts exhibited abridged Cebpb expression, correlated with augmented Pri-mir128-1 and mir128-3p compared to Mapk7flox hearts 1 week post-MI (Figure 4G and H, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4G and H, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The other two miRNAs potentially targeting Irs1 (mir144-3p and mir145-5p) and Cebpa in the myocardium were not altered by MAPK7 ablation.
source: The other two miRNAs potentially targeting Irs1 (mir144-3p and mir145-5p) and Cebpa in the myocardium were not altered by MAPK7 ablation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: Only IRS1 was reduced in Mapk7-cko hearts after 1 week LAD ligation, whereas INSR, SLC2A4 and SLC2A1 were unchanged.
source: Assessment of IRS1, INSR, SLC2A4 and SLC2A1 (also known as GLUT1 encoded by Slc2a1) expression determined that only IRS1 was reduced in Mapk7-cko hearts after 1 week LAD ligation, whereas it was unchanged in Mapk7flox hearts (Figure 4I and J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data shown in Figure 4I and J, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The response to insulin was blunted in Mapk7-cko myocardium subject to 1 week MI.
source: Therefore, the response to insulin was blunted in Mapk7-cko myocardium subject to 1 week MI (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data showing reduced insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of IRS1 and AKT in Figure 4K.

claim: Storage of glycogen was not significantly declined in Mapk7-cko hearts.
source: However, storage of glycogen was not significantly declined in Mapk7-cko hearts (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by PAS staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: IRS1 was reduced in Mapk7-knockdown ARCMs and NRCMs under short-term hypoxia.
source: Consistent with in vivo results, IRS1 was reduced in Mapk7-knockdown ARCMs and NRCMs under short-term hypoxia, while no changes were detected in the control cardiomyocytes during this period (Figure 4L and M, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and immunoblot data from ARCMs and NRCMs shown in Figure 4L and M, and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Stimulated by insulin, blocked activation of IRS1 and AKT was observed in the absence of MAPK7.
